title: Choose and provision hosting for SPA + API + Postgres
description:
Roomio needs three things hosted: a static SPA bundle, a small Node/Express API,
and a Postgres database.

Constraints worth weighing:
  - The bundle is ~600 KB gzipped of JS and pulls large 3D assets, so the static
    side really wants a CDN.
  - The API is tiny and mostly idle — anything that scales to zero is fine, but
    cold starts on a 3D app's first save are user-visible.
  - Postgres must support TLS (the app now reads PGSSLMODE) and should have
    managed backups.
  - Audience is India-first (the listings are Mumbai/Pune), so region matters for
    latency.

Also decide same-origin vs split-origin: same-origin (API under the SPA's domain)
keeps the SameSite=Lax cookie and the CSRF origin check working with zero
configuration. Split-origin means setting ALLOWED_ORIGINS and re-testing auth.

Acceptance: a written decision (provider, region, same- vs split-origin) plus a
staging environment reachable over HTTPS.
notes: 2026-10-01 (PR #27/#28, merged): the static frontend DEMO is hosted on Cloudflare Pages, project roomio-demo, production URL https://roomio-demo.pages.dev (production branch setting: roomio-main). This covers only the backend-less demo. Hosting for the full app's API + Postgres (provider, region, same- vs split-origin) is still undecided, so this stays open.

title: BLOCKER: repo ships real people’s phone numbers and FB post links
description:
`public/listings.json` contains 36 scraped Facebook rental posts. Verified
contents:
  - 21 of 36 carry real phone numbers in a `phones` array
  - 36 of 36 carry a `permalink` back to the original Facebook post
  - each carries the full original `text` of the post
  - `public/images/` holds mirrored copies of the posters' photos

Author names are NOT stored (checked: 0 of 36) — that part is already clean.

Right now this is a local app and the data sits in a private repo. Publishing it
turns it into republishing strangers' contact details, at scale, to anyone with
the URL, without their consent and with no way for them to ask us to stop. That
is a problem under India's DPDP Act, and separately it is against Meta's terms
for the scraped source.

This blocks the public launch. Nothing else in the launch epic matters until it
is resolved.

Options, roughly in order of preference:
  1. Replace the dataset with synthetic listings that keep the same shape and
     visual variety. The 3D replica work is the interesting part and it does not
     depend on the listings being real.
  2. Keep the real photos and rents, strip `phones`, `permalink` and `text`, and
     make clear in the UI that listings are illustrative.
  3. Keep real data but gate the listings feature behind a login that only we
     have. Least good — the data still ships in the bundle.

Note option 2 and 3 still leave the data in git history; if we go that way, decide
separately whether history needs rewriting.

Acceptance:
  - No phone number, permalink, or verbatim post text of a real person is served
    by the public site.
  - `CLAUDE.md` §5 updated to reflect whatever rule we settle on.
notes: 2026-10-01 (PR #27, merged): the PUBLIC DEMO at https://roomio-demo.pages.dev ships none of this data. Its build uses demo/public/ instead of public/, swaps the listing tables (listingFlats, inferredScenes) for stubs, and scripts/demo-leak-check.mjs fails the build if any Facebook URL/post id or any id/phone/permalink from public/listings.json appears in dist-demo/. The FULL APP still bundles public/listings.json and public/images/, so this bead stays OPEN until the full app's dataset is replaced or stripped.

title: Detection upload writes to local disk — breaks on any real host
description:
`POST /api/detect` writes the uploaded photo and a sidecar JSON into
`shared/requests/`, and `GET /api/detect/:id` polls `shared/results/` for a file
that a separate Python watcher writes.

That design assumes one machine with a persistent writable working directory and
the Python watcher running beside the API. On a normal host none of that holds:
  - container filesystems are ephemeral, so queued requests vanish on redeploy
  - with more than one instance, the GET usually lands on a different instance
    than the POST and never sees the result file
  - the Python watcher is not deployed at all

So on launch day this endpoint will accept uploads and then silently never
return a result.

Decide one of:
  a) Disable the scan-a-photo feature in production behind a flag, and say so in
     the UI. Cheapest, honest, no infrastructure.
  b) Move the queue to the database or an object store + a real worker.
  c) Run it synchronously in-process (only viable if inference is fast enough).

(a) is the sensible launch answer; (b) is the real answer later.

Acceptance: a public user either gets a working scan or a clear "not available"
message — never an upload that hangs forever.

title: Launch Roomio as a public website
description:
Everything required to put Roomio in front of strangers on the open internet.

Roomio today is a local-dev app: it assumes localhost, a trusted network, a
developer's Postgres, and a single machine with a writable working directory.
Publishing changes the threat model and the failure modes, and this epic tracks
that gap.

Hard blocker: the repo currently ships real people's personal data (see the PII
bead). Nothing ships until that is resolved.

Exit criteria:
  - A stranger can load the site, play with the 3D designer, and save work.
  - No real person's personal data is served.
  - Errors are visible to us, not just to the user.
  - We can restore the database and roll back a bad deploy.

title: Public demo: analytics + client error tracking (Cloudflare Web Analytics + Sentry)
description:
The public demo at https://roomio-demo.pages.dev (PR #27/#28) has no visibility: we cannot see visitor counts or the WebGL/shader crashes a stranger's GPU hits.

Scope (demo only, static, no backend):
  - Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon (cookieless) on the landing page and /tour.
  - Sentry browser SDK for client errors, wired to the demo's error boundary; capture WebGL context loss.
  - Widen the demo CSP (vite.demo.config.ts) for exactly the beacon + Sentry ingest origins, never by removing it; keep demo-leak-check green.
  - Scrub PII before send; the demo has no user data, keep it that way (no session replay of inputs).
  - Lazy/deferred load so the first-load size budget still passes.

Being implemented on branch feat/demo-analytics-footer.

Acceptance: a page view and a deliberately thrown test error both show up in the dashboards from the production demo; npm run build:demo (typecheck, leak check, size budget) passes.

Full-app error tracking and API uptime stay in roomio-pnc.7.

title: Security hardening pass: proxy, headers, CSRF, limits, TLS, shutdown
description:
Landed on branch chore/beads-tooling-and-hardening.

Fixed:
  1. trust proxy was unset. Behind any load balancer, express-rate-limit keyed
     every request into one bucket — one abuser would 429 the entire site, and
     express-rate-limit v7+ refuses to start with ERR_ERL_UNEXPECTED_X_FORWARDED_FOR.
     Now env-driven via TRUST_PROXY, defaulting to 0 so local dev cannot be spoofed.
  2. No security headers at all. Added helmet with default-src 'none' +
     frame-ancestors 'none' (correct for a JSON-only API), nosniff, no-referrer,
     and HSTS in production only.
  3. No CSRF defence beyond SameSite=Lax. Added an Origin check on POST/PUT/PATCH/
     DELETE; same-origin passes automatically, ALLOWED_ORIGINS covers split-origin.
  4. No global rate limit — only auth and detect were capped. Added a per-IP
     ceiling across all of /api.
  5. Unbounded per-user storage. Each design is up to 2MB of JSONB with client-
     chosen ids, so one account could fill the database. Added MAX_DESIGNS_PER_USER,
     counted only for NEW rows so an at-quota user can still save open work.
  6. Password policy: min 6 -> min 8, and a new 72-BYTE maximum. bcrypt ignores
     input past 72 bytes, so without the cap two different long passwords could
     share a hash. Measured with Buffer.byteLength, so multi-byte input cannot
     slip past.
  7. bcrypt cost 10 -> 12, env-tunable via BCRYPT_ROUNDS.
  8. Postgres had no TLS option. pg does not infer it from the URL, so the
     password crossed the network in plaintext on any hosted database. Added
     PGSSLMODE handling that does NOT default to rejectUnauthorized:false.
  9. No pool bounds and no pool error handler — an idle client error was an
     uncaught exception. Added both.
 10. No SIGTERM handling: every deploy severed in-flight requests and leaked
     pool sockets. Added graceful drain with a forced-exit ceiling.
 11. Removed dangerouslySetInnerHTML from src/three/Flythrough.tsx. It was fed
     only string literals so it was NOT exploitable, but it was a live HTML sink
     one interpolated room/listing name away from an XSS.
 12. npm audit fix on server/ — 11 advisories down to 7, all remaining dev-only
     except the express->qs pair (see the Express 5 bead).

Verification:
  - 16 new tests in server/test/hardening.test.js pin every control above.
  - server suite: 59 passed (43 existing + 16 new).
  - frontend: 716 passed, typecheck clean, production build clean.

Also added server/.env.example documenting every knob and which are required in
production.

Deliberately NOT done here, each filed separately: Express 5, vitest major,
email verification for signup enumeration, native bcrypt, SPA CSP.

title: Gate CI on npm audit and add secret scanning
description:
The current advisories were found by running `npm audit` by hand during a
review. Nothing in CI would have surfaced them, and nothing would stop a
credential from being committed.

Add to CI:
  - `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` across all package roots, failing
    the build. Production dependencies only — dev advisories should open a
    ticket, not block a release (see the vitest bead for why).
  - secret scanning (gitleaks or GitHub's built-in) on every PR.

Note there IS a real secret-shaped path already: `scripts/fb-cookies.txt` and
`.json` hold Facebook session cookies and are gitignored. Scanning would catch
the day someone renames one of those files.
close_reason: npm audit prod gate + gitleaks with custom FB-cookie rule; verified exit 0 post-merge

title: Upgrade vitest — critical advisory in the dev toolchain
description:
`npm audit` in server/ reports, after `npm audit fix`:

  CRITICAL  vitest        <=4.1.10   arbitrary file read + execution via the
                                     Vitest UI server
  HIGH      vite          <=6.4.2    path traversal in optimized-deps .map handling
  MODERATE  @vitest/mocker, vite-node, esbuild

All are DEV dependencies — they do not ship to users, and the vitest UI server is
only exposed when someone runs `vitest --ui`. So this is not a production
exposure, which is why it is P1 and not P0. It is still a real risk to any
developer machine running the test suite.

The fix is a vitest major (2.x → 4.x) across all eight package roots, which will
touch config APIs and possibly the workspace file format. 775 tests are the
safety net. Do it as one PR, all roots together — mixed vitest majors sharing the
root node_modules will not work.

title: Replace DDL-on-boot with real migrations
description:
`server/db.js` `initDb()` runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on every process
start. That is fine for a fresh local database and wrong for a deployed one:

  - It cannot express any change to an EXISTING table. Adding a column, changing
    a type, or adding a NOT NULL all silently do nothing, because the table
    already exists.
  - Every instance runs it concurrently on deploy.
  - It requires the application's database role to hold DDL privileges forever,
    so an SQL injection anywhere becomes a schema-drop.

Move to a migration tool (node-pg-migrate, or plain numbered SQL files with a
tiny runner — the schema is three tables, this does not need to be heavy).
Migrations run as a deploy step with an admin role; the app connects with a role
that has DML only.

Blocks safe schema evolution after launch, so worth doing BEFORE there is real
user data to migrate.
close_reason: Numbered SQL migrations + runner, no new dep; 68 server tests

title: typecheck covers only src/ — roughly a third of the code
description:
`tsconfig.json` has `"include": ["src"]`. So `npm run typecheck` — the first gate
in the green bar, in CI, and in the pre-push hook — checks 22k of ~60k lines.

Not currently typechecked:
  - `scripts/` (3.7k lines, .mjs — includes the scraper and the render pipeline)
  - `shared/lib/` (shared across islands, so errors here spread)
  - `server/` (1.7k lines of plain JS, no checkJS)
  - all six island directories, each with its own tsconfig

This means a change can pass the full green bar and still be broken in a build
script or on the server.

Plan:
  - add project references or a second tsconfig covering scripts/ and shared/
  - turn on `checkJS` for server/ with JSDoc types (the code is already well
    JSDoc'd, so this is cheaper than it sounds)
  - once it is clean, flip `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` to true

Expect a first run with a lot of errors. Land it incrementally, directory by
directory, rather than in one unreviewable commit.

title: Reclaim repo weight: 1.2 GB working copy, 584 MB of stale worktrees
description:
Measured today:
  - 1.2 GB total working copy
  - 584 MB in `.claude/worktrees/` — 27 agent worktree directories
  - 354 MB in `.git`
  - 27 `worktree-agent-*` branches
  - 81 branches already fully merged into main
  - 5 registered git worktrees still pointing at merged feature branches

This is all residue from the parallel-agent build. It makes cloning slow, `git
branch` unreadable, and grep noisy.

Clean up:
  - `git worktree remove` the 5 registered worktrees (verify each is merged first)
  - delete the `worktree-agent-*` branches
  - delete merged feature branches, keeping the `integration/*` and
    `coordinator/*` history if it is worth keeping
  - `git gc --aggressive --prune=now`
  - check whether the committed PNGs in `docs/screenshots/` (several at 2-3.5 MB)
    should be recompressed; they are legitimately needed by the README but not at
    that size

Care: verify merged status before deleting anything, and do this when no agent
worktree is in use.

title: Add ESLint + Prettier — there is currently no linter at all
description:
Verified: no eslint config, no prettier config, no editorconfig anywhere in the
tree. ~60k lines of TS/TSX/JS across 8 package roots with zero automated style or
correctness enforcement.

What this costs us right now, concretely:
  - The `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` removed in the hardening pass sat there for
    months. `react/no-danger` would have flagged it the day it was written.
  - `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` are both explicitly `false` in
    tsconfig.json, so dead code accumulates invisibly.
  - Nothing catches a floating promise, a missing React hook dependency, or
    `any` creeping in.
  - Style consistency currently depends on each agent reading neighbouring lines
    (this is literally what CLAUDE.md §3 has to tell people to do).

Suggested shape:
  - typescript-eslint, react-hooks, and react-refresh
  - the security-relevant rules as ERRORS, not warnings: react/no-danger,
    no-eval, no-implied-eval, @typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises
  - Prettier for formatting, matching the existing house style (no semicolons,
    single quotes, 2-space indent) so the first run is not a 60k-line diff
  - wire into CI and the pre-push hook

Do the formatting run as its own commit, separate from the rule adoption, so
`git blame` stays usable.
close_reason: ESLint flat config + Prettier; 4 mandated rules as errors; 725 tests

title: Database backups and a tested restore
description:
Users will save designs they care about. Right now there is no backup, and no
evidence that a restore would work.

  - Enable automated backups on the managed database.
  - Actually restore one into a scratch database and confirm the designs come
    back intact. An untested backup is not a backup.
  - Write down the retention period and the recovery steps.

title: Make the first 30 seconds work for a stranger
description:
The app was built and tested by people who know it. A cold visitor arrives with
no account, no context, and no idea that any of the 3D features exist.

Worth resolving before launch:
  - What does the landing state do? Straight into the wizard, or a demo room
    already furnished that they can immediately drag?
  - Guest mode exists (localStorage) — is it obvious that work is saved locally,
    and obvious how to keep it by signing up?
  - The deep links (?stage=, ?preset=, ?listing=) are excellent demo material and
    are currently undiscoverable.
  - Is there any moment where a first-time user sees an empty grey canvas and
    concludes it is broken?

Acceptance: watch someone who has never seen Roomio use it for five minutes
without help, and fix what stops them.

title: Verify behaviour on phones and low-end GPUs
description:
A public link is opened on a phone more often than on a desktop, especially for
an India-first rental audience. Roomio is a real-time WebGL app with ~600 KB
gzipped of JS before the 3D engine loads.

Unknowns to actually measure, not guess:
  - Does the renderer hold a usable frame rate on a mid-range Android?
  - What happens on a GPU that cannot do the realism layer — graceful downgrade
    or black screen?
  - Is the wizard usable with touch, or is it mouse-assuming?
  - Time-to-interactive on a 4G connection.

There is a `fix/responsive-mobile` branch that never merged; check whether it is
still relevant before starting from scratch.
notes: 2026-10-01: only headless Chromium has been tested, against the built public demo (desktop 1440x900 / 1920x929 and phone viewport 390x844, CSP enforced: render not blank, no console/network errors). No real phone or low-end GPU has been tested. Next step: open https://roomio-demo.pages.dev/tour on a mid-range Android, an iPhone and a low-end-GPU laptop and record frame rate, touch usability, WebGL fallback behaviour and 4G load time. This note covers the real-device test of the live demo (no separate bead).

title: Error tracking and uptime monitoring
description:
Today a production error goes to a container log nobody reads, and the app going
down would be noticed only by a user complaining.

Needed before launch:
  - Client-side error reporting. `src/ErrorBoundary.tsx` already catches React
    errors; wire it to a real sink. WebGL context loss and shader failures on
    unfamiliar GPUs are the likely top crash, and we have no way to see them.
  - Server-side error reporting from the global handler in `server/app.js`.
  - Uptime check on `GET /api/health` with an alert that reaches a phone.

Scrub PII before sending: never ship a user's email or a design payload to a
third-party error service.
notes: 2026-10-01: demo-only analytics + client error tracking is tracked separately (see related bead, in progress). This bead still covers the full app: server-side error reporting and uptime checks on /api/health.

title: Set production environment variables correctly
description:
`server/.env.example` now documents every knob. The ones whose defaults are only
safe on localhost, and which MUST be set for production:

  NODE_ENV=production   → turns on Secure cookies and HSTS
  DATABASE_URL          → the managed database
  PGSSLMODE=require     → without it the DB password crosses the network in plaintext
  TRUST_PROXY=1         → behind one load balancer. Leaving it 0 breaks per-IP
                          rate limiting; setting it too high lets a client forge
                          its own IP past the limiters. Set it to the real number
                          of proxy hops, no more.
  ALLOWED_ORIGINS       → only if the SPA is on a different origin than the API

Acceptance: a deployed staging environment where a session cookie is observed
with Secure+HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax, and the rate limiter keys on the real client
IP (verify with two different clients).

title: Privacy policy, terms, and a contact/takedown route
description:
A public site that holds user accounts needs to say what it stores and how to
get rid of it.

Minimum:
  - Privacy policy: we store email, a bcrypt password hash, and saved designs;
    sessions last 30 days; how to delete an account.
  - Terms of use.
  - A working contact address for takedown requests — needed regardless of how
    the listings PII bead is resolved, if any real-world data remains.
  - Cookie notice: the session cookie is strictly necessary, which keeps this
    short, but it should be stated.

Also: there is currently no "delete my account" path in the product. Either build
one or handle requests manually and say so.

title: Build + deploy pipeline with rollback
description:
Automate what is currently nothing: build the SPA, run migrations, deploy the
API, verify health, and be able to go back.

Should include:
  - CI builds the SPA and publishes it to the static host
  - the API deploys only if the full test suite passed
  - `GET /api/health` is checked after deploy before traffic shifts
  - a documented one-command rollback

Depends on the hosting decision.
notes: 2026-10-01 (PR #27/#28, merged): the public DEMO has a pipeline. .github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml runs on every push to main (and workflow_dispatch): npm run build:demo on Node 20 (gates: typecheck, demo leak check, size budget), then wrangler pages deploy on Node 22 as the production deployment. A failed gate uploads nothing. Rollback = Cloudflare Pages dashboard -> roomio-demo -> Deployments -> Rollback. First green run: 36921320184. Still to do: the full app/API pipeline, including the migrate step, health check before traffic shift, and one-command rollback.

title: Close remaining security gaps
description:
Follow-on work from the first hardening pass (branch
chore/beads-tooling-and-hardening), which landed: trust-proxy configuration,
helmet security headers, a cross-origin CSRF guard, a global rate limit, password
bounds, bcrypt cost 12, a per-user design quota, Postgres TLS support, pool
bounds, graceful shutdown, removal of the dangerouslySetInnerHTML sink, and 16
tests pinning all of it.

This epic holds what that pass deliberately did NOT do, because each item needs a
dependency major-version bump, a product decision, or infrastructure that does
not exist yet.

title: Pay down tech debt to production standard
description:
Roomio was built by many agents working in parallel at high speed. The result
has unusually good tests and comments, and unusually weak structural boundaries.

This epic is the repair work: automated quality enforcement that does not depend
on any one agent remembering a rule, and the removal of scaffolding that has
outlived the parallel-agent build.

Explicitly NOT in scope: rewriting working 3D/render code. The rendering and
geometry code is well tested and well commented. The debt is in tooling,
boundaries and repo hygiene, not in the product logic.

Exit criteria:
  - A lint/format/typecheck gate catches the classes of bug currently caught only
    by review.
  - `npm run typecheck` covers the whole tree, not 22k of ~60k lines.
  - A fresh clone is small enough to be pleasant to work in.

title: Land the deferred Prettier reformat (123 files) as its own commit
description:
Follow-up from roomio-zhs.1. Prettier is configured and `npm run format:check`
works, but it is deliberately NOT wired into CI or pre-push yet because the
repo has never been formatted: `format:check` currently reports 123 files,
roughly 9,090 insertions / 2,153 deletions.

Held back on purpose so the reformat lands as ONE blame-ignorable commit rather
than being smeared through unrelated PRs. CLAUDE.md §3 currently tells people to
read neighbouring lines for style; once this lands, that instruction can be
replaced with 'run npm run format'.

Steps:
  1. `npm run format` in a single commit that touches nothing else.
  2. Add its SHA to a `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file.
  3. Add `npm run format:check` to CI and .githooks/pre-push.
  4. Update CLAUDE.md §3.

The config was calibrated first: printWidth 100 was measured, not guessed —
only 927 of 27,672 lines exceed it, where 80 would rewrap ~3,000 working lines.
printWidth 120 would cut the churn to ~6,940 insertions if a smaller diff is
worth more than the convention.

title: Every worktree's server suite drops and recreates the SAME roomio_test database
description:
Found while running agents in parallel worktrees during the roomio-zhs.4 review.

server/vitest.config.js defaults TEST_DATABASE_URL to:

    postgresql://localhost/roomio_test

and test/global-setup.js DROPS and recreates that database at the start of every
run. The URL has no per-checkout component.

So every git worktree — and there can be many, .claude/worktrees/ currently holds
several agent checkouts — resolves to the SAME physical database on the same
local Postgres. Two agents running `npm test --prefix server` at overlapping
times means one drops the database out from under the other mid-suite. The
resulting failure lands on whatever assertion happened to be executing, so it
looks like a product bug in an unrelated area rather than a harness collision.

This is not hypothetical now that parallel agents are a normal workflow here
(bootstrap:worktree exists precisely to support it), and it will get worse as
more agents run concurrently.

Fix options:
  - derive the test database name from the checkout path or a short hash of it,
    keeping the *_test suffix that global-setup.js safety-rails on
  - or serialise server-suite runs behind a lock
  - or have each run use a uniquely-named throwaway database and drop it after

The *_test name check in global-setup.js must survive whatever is chosen — it is
the only thing standing between a typo and dropping the real `roomio` database.

Context: a single non-reproducible failure of 'leaves GETs alone' (expected 200)
occurred during exactly such an overlap; 11 later runs passed. Not proven to be
the cause, but this is a real collision hazard regardless. Sibling bead:
roomio-xfk.9.

title: Global rate limiter is not test-injectable — latent flaky-test source
description:
Introduced by the hardening pass (roomio-xfk.8). In server/app.js, createApp()
takes `authRateLimit` and `detectRateLimit` as options, and test/helpers.js
testApp() sets both to effectively-off (limit 10_000) so ordinary tests never
trip them.

The globalLimiter added in the same pass was NOT given that treatment:

    const globalLimiter = rateLimit({
      windowMs: intEnv('GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS', 60 * 1000),
      limit:    intEnv('GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT_MAX', 600),
    })

So every test shares a hardcoded 600-requests-per-minute ceiling that testApp()
cannot override. Today the suite is nowhere near it, so nothing fails — but the
ceiling is invisible, and the failure mode when a growing suite eventually
crosses it is an intermittent 429 on an unrelated assertion, which reads as a
product bug rather than a test-harness limit.

Fix: give it a `globalRateLimit` option exactly like the other two, and set it
effectively-off in testApp(). Keep at least one test that exercises the real
limit explicitly (ratelimit.test.js is the right home).

Context: found while investigating a single non-reproducible failure of
'cross-origin (CSRF) guard > leaves GETs alone' (expected 200) during
roomio-zhs.4 verification. 11 subsequent consecutive runs passed, so this is NOT
confirmed as that failure's cause — it is a real latent problem found while
looking. See the sibling bead about worktrees sharing one roomio_test database
for the other candidate.

title: Email verification — also closes signup account enumeration
description:
Two things, one fix.

Today `POST /api/auth/signup` returns `409 email already registered`. That lets
anyone test whether a given email has a Roomio account, one request at a time
(rate-limited to 20 per 15 min per IP, so slow but not prevented). Login is
already correctly generic — it returns the same 401 for "no such user" and "wrong
password" — so signup is the only leak.

Deliberately NOT "fixed" in the hardening pass by making signup generic: without
email verification, a generic response means a user who already has an account
gets a confusing silent no-op instead of "you already have an account, log in".
That is a worse product for a marginal gain.

The real fix is verification: signup always responds the same way and sends an
email that either confirms the new account or says "someone tried to sign up with
your address — here is a login link". Enumeration closes and the UX gets better.

Needs transactional email, which is infrastructure we do not have — hence P2 and
tied to the launch epic.

Bonus: verification also gives a lever against scripted signups (see the cost
guardrails bead).

title: Content-Security-Policy for the served SPA
description:
The hardening pass set a deliberately strict CSP — `default-src 'none';
frame-ancestors 'none'` — which is exactly right for an API that only ever emits
JSON.

If the SPA ever gets served from the same process (or once we decide how the
static host sets headers), that policy will not do: the app needs script, style,
image, font and WebGL/blob sources.

When that happens:
  - widen the policy for the document route ONLY, never by deleting it
  - the tricky parts will be `blob:` for WebCodecs video export and any inline
    style injected by the 3D libraries
  - avoid `unsafe-inline` on scripts; use a nonce if something genuinely needs it

Also decide where the SPA's headers come from — the static host's config, not the
API — and put them under review like any other config.

CLAUDE.md §2 already says this policy must be widened rather than removed.
notes: 2026-10-01 (PR #27, merged): the public demo has its own CSP, a <meta> injected at build time by vite.demo.config.ts (so preview:demo enforces the same policy), plus demo/public/_headers (frame blocking, nosniff, referrer policy). demo-leak-check fails the build if index.html ships without the CSP. The full SPA's CSP is still open.

title: Express 5 migration to clear the qs advisories
description:
The only remaining PRODUCTION dependency advisories:

  MODERATE  qs 2.2.5-6.15.3  array-limit bypass; DoS via attacker-controlled isBuffer
  MODERATE  express 4.22.2   depends on the vulnerable qs

express 4.22.2 is the last of the 4.x line, so there is no patch to take — the
fix is Express 5.

Impact on us is limited: `qs` parses query strings, and Roomio's API takes almost
everything in the JSON body or the path. Worth doing, not worth rushing.

Express 5 changes: async error handling (our `wrap()` helper becomes partly
redundant), removal of some route-path patterns, and `req.query` becoming a
getter. The 59-test server suite covers the surface well enough to make this a
safe change.

title: Move off bcryptjs to a native hash implementation
description:
`server/auth.js` uses `bcryptjs` — a pure-JavaScript bcrypt. It is correct, but
it is roughly an order of magnitude slower than a native implementation for the
same work factor, and it runs on the API's only thread.

The hardening pass raised the cost from 10 to 12, which is the right security
call but multiplies that CPU time by four. Under a burst of logins this is the
most likely way to stall the event loop — worth confirming in the load-test bead
before deciding urgency.

Options:
  - `@node-rs/bcrypt` — native bcrypt, same hashes, so existing password hashes
    keep verifying and no migration is needed. Lowest risk.
  - `argon2id` — better algorithm, but existing bcrypt hashes must be rehashed
    on next successful login, which is more code and a migration window.

Recommend @node-rs/bcrypt for the drop-in, and treat argon2 as a separate call.
Keep BCRYPT_ROUNDS env-tunable either way.

title: Automate dependency updates
description:
Renovate or Dependabot, so security advisories surface as PRs instead of being
found by someone running `npm audit` by hand — which is how the current batch was
found.

Configure it for all eight package roots, and group the three-ecosystem packages
(three, @react-three/*, postprocessing) since they must move together.

title: Measure test coverage
description:
716 frontend tests and 59 server tests, and no idea what fraction of the code
they touch. Coverage is not a goal in itself, but right now we cannot answer
"is this module tested?" without reading it.

  - turn on vitest's coverage reporter across the workspace
  - publish the summary in CI
  - once there is a baseline, set a floor that blocks a drop

Expect the 3D/render code to be worse covered than the geometry and persistence
code, which is fine — the useful output is knowing WHERE the gaps are.

title: CI bundle-size budget
description:
`npm run build` currently emits `three-core` at 1,036 KB (312 KB gzipped) and an
index chunk at 1,078 KB (315 KB gzipped) — roughly 600 KB gzipped of JS on first
meaningful load.

The chunking is carefully tuned (see the long comment in vite.config.ts about
virtual modules un-splitting the bundle), and there is nothing stopping a future
change from silently undoing it. A typecheck and a passing test suite will not
notice.

Add a CI step that fails when a chunk crosses a threshold, so the split stays
split. Pair with CLAUDE.md §8.
close_reason: scripts/size-check.mjs; catches the un-split via eager-closure walk, verified exit 1

title: Dissolve the six-island layout back into src/ + shared/lib
description:
`camera-flythrough/ lighting/ multi-room/ persistence/ rendering/ texturing/` are
each a sibling directory with their own package.json, vite config, vitest config
and build output, all imported by the app in `src/`.

This is scaffolding from the parallel-agent build — it let agents work without
colliding. It is not a design anyone would choose, and it now costs:

  - `vite.config.ts` needs an 11-entry `resolve.dedupe` list to stop duplicate
    copies of React/three loading. Getting it wrong produces "Hooks can only be
    used within the Canvas component" at RUNTIME with a clean typecheck.
  - Eight package.json files must keep dependency versions in lockstep by hand.
  - `npm run bootstrap:worktree` exists purely to symlink node_modules around
    this layout.
  - Shared logic gets copy-pasted between islands instead of living in one place.

This is the largest structural debt in the repo and the one most likely to be
done wrong in a hurry. Do it one island at a time, each behind a green bar, each
its own PR. Every island has its own test suite — those tests are the safety net,
so move them with the code and keep them passing.

CLAUDE.md §7 forbids adding new islands in the meantime.

title: Cost guardrails and abuse budget
description:
A public site with unauthenticated endpoints and image hosting can generate a
bill. Before launch, decide what the ceiling is and how we find out we are
approaching it.

  - Billing alerts on the hosting and database.
  - What is the plan if someone scripts thousands of signups? (Rate limits cap
    request volume, but not account creation over time — each account can hold
    up to MAX_DESIGNS_PER_USER designs at 2 MB each.)
  - Bandwidth cost of serving listing photos and 3D assets from the CDN.

title: Load-test the API before launch
description:
The rate limits and the pool bound (PG_POOL_MAX=10) were chosen by reasoning,
not by measurement. Before a public launch, find out what actually happens under
load.

Worth knowing:
  - Where does the API fall over — connection pool, event loop, or database?
  - Is bcrypt at cost 12 a bottleneck under a burst of logins? (bcryptjs is pure
    JS; this is the main argument for the native/argon2 migration bead.)
  - Do the rate limits trigger at a sane point for real users rather than only
    for attackers?

title: Watch CI after GitHub's ubuntu-latest moves to Ubuntu 26 (from 2026-10-19)
description:
GitHub-hosted runners start moving ubuntu-latest to Ubuntu 26 from 2026-10-19. Every job in ci.yml and deploy-demo.yml runs on ubuntu-latest, so the image can change under us without a commit.

After that date, check the first CI and 'Deploy public demo' runs on main: setup-node (Node 20 for build/tests, Node 22 for wrangler), the postgres:16 service container used by the server-test job, and the wrangler upload step.

If something breaks: pin runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 as a stopgap, then fix forward.

Acceptance: one green CI run and one green demo deploy on the new image, or a pinned runner with a follow-up bead.

title: Two more pointless dynamic imports: personas.ts and listings.ts
description:
Found while fixing roomio-zhs.10 (which cleared the listingFlatLauncher case).

`npm run build` still warns about the same pattern twice more:

  src/data/personas.ts — dynamically imported by App.tsx, statically imported by
    store.ts AND wizard/StyleStart.tsx
  src/data/listings.ts — dynamically imported by App.tsx, statically imported by
    wizard/Listings.tsx

In both cases the dynamic import buys nothing: an eager static importer already
pulls the module into the first-load graph, so the import() only implies a split
that never happens.

Note the measurement from zhs.10 before assuming this is worth much: splitting
listingFlatLauncher for real moved ~2 kB gzipped out of a ~99 kB gzipped first
load, because the surrounding graph is eager regardless. Expect the same order of
magnitude here. The value is mostly in removing a misleading signal — a build
warning everyone learns to ignore is a warning that hides the next real one.

Either make the static importers lazy too, or drop the dynamic import and keep
the static one (what zhs.10 chose, with the reasoning in a comment in App.tsx).

title: Session management: invalidate other sessions, let users see them
description:
Sessions last 30 days and there is no way to end one except from the browser
that created it.

Gaps:
  - There is no password-change endpoint yet, but when there is, it must delete
    every other session for that user. Otherwise "change your password" does not
    evict someone who already has your cookie — the exact situation where a user
    changes their password.
  - No "log out everywhere".
  - No visibility into active sessions.

Low priority until there is a password-change flow, but that flow must not ship
without the invalidation. Filing now so it is not forgotten then.

title: Build warning: listingFlatLauncher is both statically and dynamically imported
description:
`npm run build` prints:

    listingFlatLauncher.ts is dynamically imported by src/App.tsx but also
    statically imported by src/wizard/Listings.tsx — dynamic import will not move
    module into another chunk.

So the dynamic import in App.tsx buys nothing: the static import from Listings.tsx
pulls it into the eager graph anyway. Either make Listings.tsx import it lazily
too, or drop the dynamic import in App.tsx and stop implying a split that is not
happening.

Small, but it is exactly the kind of thing that makes the bundle-budget bead
harder to reason about later.
close_reason: Dropped the dynamic import in App.tsx; measured both options first

title: Stale comment: server suite is described as not yet landed
description:
`vitest.workspace.ts` line 25:

    // './server/vitest.config.ts' — WI-3 is adding a server suite; slot it in here when it lands.

The server suite landed a while ago and now has 59 tests. It is correctly kept
OUT of the root workspace (it needs Postgres, and the root suite must run with
nothing but `npm ci`) and CI gates it in a separate job.

So the exclusion is right and the comment is wrong — it reads as an oversight and
invites someone to "fix" it by adding the suite to the workspace, which would
break `npm test` for anyone without a local Postgres.

Rewrite it to say why the suite is deliberately separate.
close_reason: Comment rewritten; server suite correctly stays out of the workspace
